description: The curse that damns the dragonkin, and the story's central engine. The dragonkin were once a fierce dragon-blooded warrior people. In an act of hubris they warred upon the divine -- turning their strength against a god (of earth and living things) and were cast down. The curse is inherited: those who carry the blood carry the sentence, paying for an ancestral crime they never chose. It rhymes deliberately with the knight's own oath -- one binding freely sworn, the other imposed by blood. The god they assailed became the instrument of their punishment: the very land now rejects them.
rules: The curse has four terms, absolute and uncurable -- no cure, no loophole, no expiation. (1) WANDER: the dragonkin can never hold a home. (2) DEFENSE ONLY: their strength may only shield, never conquer. They CAN still strike in aggression -- the curse does not make it impossible -- but every aggressive act deepens the curse, accelerating the Ashing and the wandering. Aggression is thus possible, and self-destructive: a standing temptation that damns them faster. (3) THE ASHING: wherever they linger too long, the land itself rejects them and dies, turning to desolate desert -- the assailed god's retribution, worked through the earth. (4) CONTAGION: anyone who fully casts their lot with the tribe inherits the WHOLE curse -- wandering, defense-only, and the Ashing alike. The permanence is load-bearing: the tragedy must be fixed, not solvable.

details.The sin: Hubris on a cosmic scale. The dragon-blooded warriors, drunk on victory, turned their strength against the divine itself -- a god of earth and living things -- and were cast down for it. The living dragonkin inherit the sentence for a war they never fought.
details.Why the land, specifically: They warred on a god of earth/life, so the punishment is worked through the ground: it will not hold them, and dies to be rid of them. Victim became jailer.
details.The Ashing (mechanism): Land-rejection is gradual, not instant -- long enough to raise a semblance of life, never long enough to keep it. Working timeframe: roughly a season before the blight sets in and the ground begins turning to ash and desert. This is WHY kingdoms 'ask them to leave' -- their presence desertifies the borderland, giving the crown an honest, non-villainous reason to expel them.
details.Defense only (enforcement): Not a physical bar and not mere compulsion -- aggression is possible but costly. To strike first, to make war, to conquer, deepens the curse: the Ashing comes faster, the road grows crueler. A warrior people are therefore tempted every time they are threatened to save themselves by damning themselves. For a joined knight, his trained aggression -- his entire craft -- becomes the thing that most harms the people he loves.
details.Contagion (scope): Full transfer. One who joins the tribe and casts their lot with them takes on the entire curse: they wander, their strength turns defense-only under the same penalty, and the land begins to die where they rest. To choose the dragonkin is to be damned with them -- not to escape into love but to inherit a sentence.
details.Thematic function: A warrior people forbidden war; a homeless people who blight any home; a curse for a broken oath against heaven -- set beside a knight whose identity is his oath and his sword. The curse is the mirror the whole book turns on, and the title's two halves: the ASH they leave, the OATH they broke.
